form_note: dominus written as d+o ligature followed by a raised hooked stroke (ꝰ-like) with a dot beneath it, not the usual dñs; in Ave Maria ... dominus tecum
z-shaped et sign for final -m at line end; sits on the line, tail just below baseline [z-shaped ꝫ after a letter other than q; here = final -m]
deo written as round d fused with o, with a small hooked/curled mark sitting on top of the o next to the ascender tip (does not cross the ascender); possibly the scribe's d-stroke variant
p with a short hairline mark above the bowl for prae-; descender curls left
same d+o+hooked raised stroke for dominus (Quoniam deus magnus dominus), followed by a darker-ink colon
p whose descender sweeps in a long hairline curve down-left below the line (pro loop)
9-shaped superscript after m at line end; small open loop + taller right stroke
z-shaped sign for final -m after a [z-shaped ꝫ after a letter other than q; here = final -m]
dominus as d+o ligature + small raised hook at the ascender top whose hairline tail curves down to the baseline; same form as f.11r
deus written as round d followed by a round-s-like sign with a flag/curl at its top (no ꝰ, no macron); directly after the dominus abbreviation
final -m sign at line end with a long hairline tail running down-left below the line [z-shaped ꝫ after a letter other than q; here = final -m]
p with a hairline descender crossed by a slanting hairline bar just below the baseline
p with no real descender: stem ends in a foot turned left plus a diagonal hairline; reading forced by sense (pximus)
small raised hook above-right of t at line end for -er
propter written p+ter only: a p whose stem ends in a foot hairline turned left (same foot-p as in super/perfecisti), so the pro value is not marked by a distinct loop; reading by sense
final e carries a comma-shaped hook at its lower right whose hairline runs below the line; apparently stands for final -m (no macron, no ꝫ)
quod written as q plus a raised diagonal tick at x-height right of the bowl (no stroke through the descender)
eius as e + a small hooked head at x-height whose long hairline tail runs down-left below the baseline; followed by colon at line end; much longer tail than the 9-shaped ꝰ in procidamus (f.11r)
hook-headed hairline after n at line end, same long-tailed ꝰ as in eius above
z-shaped ꝫ for final -m at line end, tail runs well below the line
tuarum ends u+ꝫ (final -m) rather than with the rum sign ꝝ; line end, followed by a line-filler flourish
-bus as b + a raised wedge at the top right with a hairline tail down to the baseline (ꝰ-like, could also be read as the b; form); squeezed against the right margin
que sign: upper diamond + lower comma stroke, separate from q
quorum ends u+ꝫ (final -m) at line end, not ꝝ

r rotunda after o with an almost vertical hairline dropping from its foot well below the line (not a slanting cross-stroke); followed by colon at line end; same page writes eorum also in full (l.4) and as eoruꝫ (l.6)
eorum as eoru+ꝫ (final -m) at line end, two lines below eoꝝ: same word abbreviated differently on one page
q with a zigzag (tilde-like) bar above and a small hooked stroke on its right shoulder, possibly superscript a: q(u)a(m)
upper dot + lower comma, close to the q bowl
z-shaped ꝫ for final -m mid-line
ꝫ for final -m; upper stroke small, lower tail short and curved
p with a small diamond-shaped stroke above the stem for prae-
sanctus as ſ-c-s with a long straight hairline bar running from the top of c across above the final round s (not a wavy tilde), with a small dot under the bar; at line end
p written with a short stem and a long horizontal hairline foot running left along the baseline; no other mark for per-, so the foot is taken as the per bar
r rotunda after u (not o) with a straight hairline dropping from its foot below the line; line end
diamond-shaped dot above the p for prae-
tuo written tu + a small raised o-like curl at x-height top, squeezed between u and the long s of semper
in RED rubric ink: ꝰ after l with an open bowl and a long tail curving down below the line; also stands for -mus, not just -us
h with a horizontal bar through the top of its ascender (h-stroke) for hab-; structurally the same device as d_stroke but on h
diamond-shaped dot above the p for prae-
p whose foot hairline sweeps down-left into a closed loop below the line (pro loop); compare the short-foot p used for proximus on f.11v
ꝫ for final -m in the contraction mīa(m) = misericordiam
RED rubric: a followed by a hooked stroke at x-height whose hairline runs down-left below the line (ꝫ/ꝰ-like); stands for antiphona; elsewhere the rubric is a with a bar (ā)
animarum as aīaru+ꝫ (final -m) at line end, not aīaꝝ
short-stemmed p with a hairline bar slanting under/through the foot of the stem just below the baseline
omnium as o + ī + ꝫ at line end: the ꝫ stands for -um (i.e. -ium with the dotted/marked i), not just -m
lone p at line end for per- of perducat, followed by a faint double-hairline hyphen; the only per marking is the short stem with a leftward foot hairline
small diamond/tick raised above c (between c and final e) standing for -er- in benedic(er)e; looks like a dot rather than a curl
RED rubric (Lectio prima): p with a short raised tick above the stem for -ri-
ur-curl: small 2-shaped hook raised above the final u
ꝫ for final -m at line end, compact, tail short
cuius written cu+ꝰ (no i); ꝰ is a hook at x-height with a long hairline tail curving down below the baseline
ꝫ for final -m; upper bar short, tail long running below the line
-bus as b + a raised curved hook leaning right from the top of the b ascender (no tail), squeezed at the right margin; same device as mulieribꝰ f.12v
ꝓ standing alone as the word pro: p whose foot hairline swings down-left in an open loop below the line
ꝫ for final -m, mid-line
ꝰ after n: open hook at x-height with a hairline tail sweeping down-left; contrast the d+o+hook form of dominus on f.11r/11v
ꝰ raised high above x-height after p at line end, small comma-like hook with short tail
ꝓ for the word pro (pro salute), written tight against the following word; foot loop sweeps down-left
ꝰ high above x-height after m, comma-shaped hook pointing right
ur-curl: small faint tick above the last minim of u, partly hidden by the initial's frame
patrem as p + r rotunda + e under a long bar, then ꝫ (final -m) fused to the e: the e ends in a hooked tail descending at its right; at line end. Same construction as p̄reꝫ on f.18v
standalone et sign (cherubin ꝫ seraphin) drawn as two separate short horizontal wedges, one above the other, with almost no diagonal joining them; only about 2/3 x-height
pro sign written detached from the rest of the word (ꝓ clamāt), foot hairline looping down-left
ꝰ after e with a very long hairline tail curling down to ~25 px below the baseline (g-like at a glance)

full x-height 9-shape (closed bowl top-left, stem to baseline, long hairline tail curling below the line) after e at line end: here ꝰ stands for -rus, and it is as large as a con sign ꝯ rather than superscript
ꝑ for the word per (Te per orbem): stem descends, slanting hairline bar crosses it just below the baseline
ꝫ for final -m at line end
ꝫ for final -m
quoque written only as q + que sign (q;), squeezed at the right margin; the sign is a small hooked 2-shape with no separate dot
standalone z-shaped sign (like ꝫ) after sempiternus where the text requires es; preceded by a looping hairline flourish; at line end. Either ꝫ used for es, or a line filler with es omitted
ꝫ for final -m
small raised hook above the junction of t and final round s, standing for -ri- (not -er-) in patris; line end
que sign at line end: diamond dot over a comma whose tail runs down-left past the baseline; nearly touches the q bowl
ꝰ after m at line end; loop open, tail curving down to the baseline; compare laudamꝰ on f.15r where the sign is a small comma
ꝰ fused to the last minim of m: a raised hook at the top right and a hairline tail descending below the line, so the end of the word looks like 'my'
textbook 9-shaped con: closed oval bowl upper left, thick stroke down the right to the baseline, hairline tail running down-left below the line; full x-height
dominus as d+o ligature + raised hook whose long hairline tail curls down to the baseline and below, at line end (same form as f.11r/11v)
diamond dot above the p for prae-
tua written t + superscript a, at the extreme right of the line
ꝰ after t at line end drawn full x-height (bowl at x-height, stem to baseline, tail curling below), the size of a letter rather than a superscript
dominus as d+o + raised hook with a thin S-curved hairline tail descending to below the baseline; followed by a colon framed with hairline loops (line-filler)

rum sign after e (dieꝝ), not after o: r rotunda with a hairline that starts inside the glyph near the baseline and drops in a long curve to ~25 px below the line; colon framed in hairline loops follows
ipse written i-p-e with a straight bar over p/e standing for the omitted s; the same word is written in full (ipſe) a few words earlier on the same line
que sign in the z-shaped ꝫ form (not dot+comma); its upper stroke joins the top right of the q bowl
er curl as a small hook above-right of the final t at line end
standalone et sign (tuam ꝫ gloriam) made of two separate short wedges with a hairline link, sitting high (top at x-height top, bottom ~10 px above baseline); smaller than x-height
ꝫ attached directly to t (ſtratꝫ) standing for -um, not just -m; the t's crossbar runs into the top of the sign so they look like one glyph; line end
rum sign after a (tuaꝝ), at the right margin: r rotunda with a flick at the top right and a hairline crossing its foot down-left below the line
post written as p + a raised curved stroke above-right of the bowl (like a superscript o/hook), alone at line end (adhesit anima mea p(ost) te)
ꝫ for final -m pressed against the right margin; narrow (13 px) and its hairline tail runs straight down ~25 px below the baseline
nostri as noſt + a raised hooked/looped stroke above-right of t (superscript i / -ri); compare nr̄i (bar) for the same word two lines below
ꝫ for final -m; tall (37 px) with strong diagonal
tibi written t + a small raised i-like hook above the t (superscript i); same line has tibi in full a line below
q + a 2/z-shaped sign (same look as the que sign) that the text requires to be read quia (letentur et exultent gentes quia iudicas), i.e. the qꝛ = quia abbreviation; long hairline tail; at line end
te written as t + a raised thick wedge with a hairline flick up-right, above the t at the right margin (superscript e)
p with a short stem whose foot turns left, crossed by a long thin hairline running from lower left (x 618) up-right under the bowl; same per form as oꝑa on f.11v
super written ſ + r with a straight bar over the r (ſr̄), not the per sign; elsewhere super is written in full (f.12r, f.13r)

round d whose back sends a hairline up-right to a detached diamond wedge above-right of the ascender tip (wedge at 322-333,1064-1079); the stroke does not cross the ascender, it springs from it; preceded by n with a long bar
bene + a small raised c-shaped stroke above the final e at the right margin, apparently truncating benedicite (elsewhere this canticle uses bn̄)

round d with a short thick comma-like stroke detached above-right of its ascender tip (312-320,1295-1311), parallel to the ascender; does not cross it. Same function as Bn̄đ six lines up but a different mark shape (no hairline, no diamond)
word broken ſup|exaltet: the line-end p has a short stem ending on the baseline in a left foot (no descender, no visible bar), so the per value is carried only by the foot-p form

d+o followed by a raised closed loop with a stem (ꝰ-like), squeezed at the right margin before a colon; the text requires domino (germinantia in terra domino), not dominus: the same mark as in dō(ꝰ)=dominus on f.11r/11v/16v stands here for -mino
standalone et (cete ꝫ omnia): two separate wedges, upper one smaller, linked by a hairline at the left that runs down below the line
hominum as h-o-ī-ꝫ: the ꝫ stands for -um (with ī for -min-)
patrem as p̄ + r + e + ꝫ: the ꝫ grows directly out of the e (e's tongue forms its upper stroke) so e and ꝫ are one glyph; compare pr̄eꝫ on f.15r
standalone et (patrem ꝫ filium), two wedges with hairline, close in size to the -m ꝫ just before it
eius as e + a flag-like hook on the e's top right with a hairline falling to the baseline; the ꝰ is barely distinct from the e (cf. the clearer eꝰ on f.12r); line end before colon
ꝫ for final -m drawn as two separate wedges (upper short, lower a curved stroke) with almost no diagonal; compact

que written as a single q whose stem rises above x-height into a left-hooked flag and whose descender is crossed by a horizontal bar near its foot (ꝗ-type); at line end, the text requires que (aque omnes que super celos sunt). Not the usual q; form
sunt written ſ + t with a detached diamond above-right of the t at the right margin (no macron); reading forced by context (creata sunt)
er sign as a detached teardrop/comma floating above the t (not joined to it), well above the ascender line
final s at line end written like ꝰ (hook at x-height, hairline tail curling below the line) after a full u, so it is a round-s variant, not the us sign; easily confused with ꝰ
C is the painted initial; the con macron is a brown-ink wedge running right from the initial's top across over the o (1050-1076, y 512-522), easy to mistake for part of the initial frame
-um shown by a hooked stroke rising from the top of the final c into a detached teardrop above the line, at the right margin (cantic' novum)

standalone et (tympano ꝫ psalterio): upper wedge and lower wedge joined by a thin diagonal, plus a long hairline from the upper wedge curving down-left below the line; squeezed between two words with no spacing
gloria written g + a raised open curl (superscript a?) floating above and right of the g at line end; g's top bar is long and flat; hairline from the g bowl sweeps down-left
ꝰ after i as a small comma-shaped hook with a long thin tail sweeping down-left through the line; followed by a period
ꝫ for final -m joined to the e: the e's tongue runs straight into the ꝫ's upper stroke, so e+ꝫ look like one 'ez' ligature
standalone et (tympano ꝫ choro): upper and lower wedges with a hairline loop at left that descends below the line; small, top below x-height top
ꝫ for final -m mid-line; tall, its lower stroke ends in a hook below the baseline
ꝫ standing for -et (laudꝫ = laudet, Omnis spiritus laudet dominum) at line end, with a detached dot above it; not -m or -um here
ꝫ for final -m; compact, upper stroke a diamond
con sign: open-topped bowl at upper left (bowl not fully closed, looks like a narrow 9/g), stroke down to the baseline and a hairline tail curving down-left to ~15 px below the line
diamond dot above p standing for -re- inside the word (de-p(re)-cationes), same mark as the prae- sign; p written with a short stem and a long baseline foot
ſꝫ = sed (sed a periculis cunctis libera nos): z-shaped sign after long s, its tail runs ~15 px below the line; placed right after a punctus with no space
ꝫ for final -m at line end, long tail
er shown by a hairline rising from the right end of the t crossbar to above x-height (with a small knob), at the right margin
que sign in z-form (ꝫ), detached from the q bowl
semper written ſemp with no letters after p; p has a short stem, foot to the left and a hairline that crosses below the bowl - the only mark for -er
patri as pat + a raised wedge sitting above the t at line end (superscript i, standing for -ri)
Christo written as x (chi) + superscript o, a small closed o perched on the right arm of the x
word-final s at line end drawn like ꝰ: hook at x-height, then a hairline tail curling ~35 px below the baseline; follows a full u, so it is an s variant (same as exaltatus f.19v)
Israel contracted to iſrl with a slanting bar running from the top of the r across the l ascender (l-stroke), like the d_stroke device applied to l
sunt written ſt + a raised hook joined to the top of the t and curling back left (like an er/ur curl), at line end; contrast ſtᵒ (diamond) for sunt on f.19r
pro sign: p whose foot hairline runs left along the baseline and sweeps down-left below it; followed by ph with a long bar over -het-
ꝫ for final -m; ink-heavy upper diamond, tail descending below the line
nostrum as n + r + ꝫ (no bar): ꝫ here = -um after the contracted nr; at line end before a colon, tail long
ꝰ drawn full-size at x-height (closed bowl, stem to baseline, short tail) after b at the line end - same size as a con sign, not superscript
ꝰ written as a raised hooked flag sitting on top of the e and above x-height, with a thin tail curving down the right side of the e; squeezed at the right margin, much like eꝰ on f.19r
ꝫ for final -m directly attached to the e (tongue of e becomes the upper stroke)
ꝫ for final -m at line end, tail running down below the line
ꝓ as the word pro (pro nobis), written tight against nobis; the hairline from the foot loops down-left and back up under the bowl into a near-closed loop
ur curl as a flat wavy stroke above the last minims of m (more like a tilde than a 2-shaped curl)
per: p with a short stem and a hairline that crosses the stem foot diagonally, running down-left to ~15 px below the baseline
ꝫ for final -m fused to e, hairline tail swings down then right below the line; the word also has ō for -on-
ꝫ for final -m, narrow; immediately followed (touching) by the red response sign ℟
per: p with a foot running left along the baseline and a second hairline crossing below it (double foot), looks like a small 'z' under the p
gloriosa split glꝉi|osa: the l ascender is crossed by a short horizontal stroke for -or- (l-stroke), same device as đ but on l; line end
per: p with short stem and foot; a hairline crosses the foot diagonally and runs down-left ~15 px below the baseline
Sancta at line end written as ſ + a small raised c/a cluster beside its shoulder, squeezed against the margin after oms
semper as ſ + p, with the ſ's head flag extended into a long bar over the p; the p's descender also ends in a hairline swinging left; abbreviated differently from ſemꝑ (f.20v) and full ſemper (f.21r)
ꝓ joined to nobis with no space; the foot hairline sweeps down-left in a long curve to ~20 px below the line
diamond dot above the p for prae-; the p is preceded by a punctus and written without space
que sign in z-form, its upper wedge touching the q bowl
standalone q + z-shaped ꝫ; the text needs quoque here (martyrum quoque omnium), as with q; on f.15v, though qꝫ would normally be -que; ambiguous
con sign tall and narrow (closed bowl at upper left, stem down to baseline, hairline tail to ~10 px below); ink faint; preceded closely by et
que in z-form at line end, the q and ꝫ touching
que in z-form written as a separate word (bonis qꝫ) - the q is detached from bonis
ꝓ: foot hairline turns into a closed loop under the bowl, then a long hairline running left
pro loop under the p bowl reaching left to the preceding word's last letter; the bottom of the loop touches the frame of the initial below
ꝓ: the foot hairline crosses back right under the bowl and then sweeps far left below the line (open loop)
que in z-form; upper wedge touches q, lower stroke ends in a hairline hook
dominum as d + n̄ + ꝫ: the ꝫ stands for -um (Per dominum) at line end
RED rubric: ad p + a red z-shaped sign with a long descending hairline tail; seems to stand for -m(am) of primam (ꝫ in rubric ink)
ꝫ for final -m after e; very long hairline tail curling ~25 px below the baseline into a hook, the longest -m tail in this range
ꝰ reduced to a raised curved hook sitting above-right of the final minim, no tail below; squeezed against the right margin
tua as t + a raised wedge/hook (superscript a) at the right margin
ꝫ for final -m; compact, no tail below the line
ꝫ for final -m; narrow (16 px) with a straight hairline tail dropping to ~15 px below the line; followed by a punctus
ꝓ: thick foot stroke running left from the stem, then a hairline doubling back down-left (two-part loop)
final -us at line end shown only by a u whose last stroke runs on as a long hairline ~30 px below the baseline (no hook/bowl); reading forced by the psalm text (incolatus meus prolongatus est)
ꝫ for final -m at line end; upper part a short wedge, lower part a curved stroke ending in a hairline tail
ꝫ for final -m; small, upper wedge and a lower comma, hardly any diagonal
que in z-form at line end, upper wedge almost touching q, compressed against the margin
que in z-form; upper wedge joined to q's bowl top by a hairline
ꝰ after n as a closed loop at x-height with the stroke continuing down to the baseline and a hairline tail curling left (9-shape), not superscript
dominus as d+o + a 9-shaped ꝰ with closed bowl and stem to the baseline, full x-height size; at line end. The same line writes Dominꝰ fully just before: two abbreviations of the same word on one line
pro: the foot hairline makes a wide open loop down-left, reaching the left margin rule
que in z-form; upper wedge large, set slightly apart from q
ꝫ for final -m; the preceding word is also tuum but written with a final m (tuū/tuum) - same word written two ways side by side
que in z-form, small, sits low
que written as q with a straight macron (q̄) instead of the que sign (in his que dicta sunt)
ꝫ for final -m, followed immediately by dn̄i
ꝫ after p standing for -sum (id ipꝫ = idipsum): an unexpected syllable for this sign; the ꝫ touches the p's bowl
ꝫ for final -m in enim; the minims before it are hard to count, so the word may be eñꝫ

tribus written t + b + a large 9-shaped ꝰ (closed bowl, stem, long tail with a detached stroke below the line), with no mark for the omitted -ri-; the same word is written in full just before it (tribus tribus)
cō at line end with a long flat bar over the o (1130-1170, y 683-692) that extends past the o to the right margin; word continues fitendum on the next line
que as q with macron at line end (Rogate que ad pacem sunt), second q̄=que on this page
ierusalem contracted to ierlm with a long bar from the r across the l ascender (l-stroke); same device as iſrl̄ (f.21r)
eius reduced to e + a small raised hook at the top right (no tail), written touching the preceding mīa with no word space at the right margin
seculum as ſecl + ꝫ (ꝫ = -um), the l ascender with a bar; line end. The same phrase in seculum is written in full (ſeculum) two lines above
second ſeclꝫ = seculum at line end, identical construction

round d with a detached diamond wedge set above-right of its ascender tip (733-745, y 873-886), not crossing it; here it stands for -er- (confid-er-e), whereas the similar mark on d in Bn̄đ (f.18r) truncates benedicite; con- in the same word is written out in full
quam as q + a small superscript a (looped) on the q's shoulder, with a tilde-like flick over the bowl
second qͣ = quam on this page; the superscript a is fused to the top of the q stem and the q's descender ends in a hairline flourish
quia written q + r-like sign (straight r with diamond head) at line end; compare f.17v where qꝛ=quia uses a z-shaped sign like the que sign
domini as round d + o with the d's ascender curling over the o (plus a small tick at its end) at line end; the same d+o+mark shape stands for dominus on f.11r/11v/16v and domino on f.18v
z-shaped et sign for final -m after e, hairline tail runs down-left to x1150 below baseline; followed by colon; z/semicolon sign after a letter other than q, here = final -m
standalone et-sign squeezed at line end after 'dñs:' (et morti...); small, lighter ink, a vertical hairline (ruling/pen trace) passes just left of it
line-end 'porta domini' written as round d + o with a hairline rising up-right from the o (suspension for -mini); not the usual dñi
z-sign for -um at line end of 'a dño fc̄ꝫ'; long macron over fc, z tail curls far below line to y1338; z/semicolon sign after a letter other than q, here = final -m
in noīe d(omini) at line end: round d whose bowl is closed by a stroke rising above x-height to the upper right; a single-letter suspension for domini (cf. 'dō' with separate o elsewhere)
z-sign for final -m after e, long S-curved tail down-left below baseline; z/semicolon sign after a letter other than q, here = final -m
9-shaped con sign, closed bowl top-left, hairline tail down-left below baseline to y562; the word is spelled with intrusive p (ꝯdēp|sis = condempsis) and divided over the line end
z-shaped que sign after q, hairline tail runs straight down to y627 parallel to the q descender; typical form
tibi suspended at line end as t with a raised comma-like i above to the right; compare tᶦ on f. 35v
mihi as m with a small raised diamond-and-hook (superscript i) above its last minims
'Confitemini d(omin)o:' at line end: round d + o with a stroke rising from the o to above the x-height, touching the colon
z-sign for -m after a; compact with almost no tail, touching the a; the same word is written 'quoniam' in full at y760 and 'q̄m' at the next line
que sign drawn as a closed 8 (two stacked loops) at x-height instead of the usual z with a descending tail, with a macron over the q; unique form in this range
que written as q with a macron (not the q; sign) in 'requiem q̄siui'

small et sign between 'quesivi' and 'in' drawn as two diamonds joined by a hairline (z reduced to a dotted form); a pale looped hairline is drawn just left of it (x820-835, y1080-1128), the same added loop seen beside et signs on ff. 36r, 36v, 37r
small hooked vertical stroke (superscript i/t) above x for dixit
z-sign for -um at line end after o + i with long macron; tail descends to y1250; z/semicolon sign after a letter other than q, here = final -m
z-sign for final -m after a, line end; z/semicolon sign after a letter other than q, here = final -m
pre- written as p with a small apostrophe-like hook above its bowl (x293-302, y1363-1378); the p's foot runs left at the baseline with a hairline below; reading preelegit
z-sign for final -m after a; touches the red response sign that follows; z/semicolon sign after a letter other than q, here = final -m
p with leftward foot-bar and crossing hairline standing for par- (post partum); same weak per-bar form as permansisti
z-sign for final -m after u in post partum; tail detached and running down-left to y338

per marked only by the p's foot-stroke extending left through the stem with a hairline running down-left; nearly identical to plain p in this hand (cf. supplicibus), so the per-bar is weakly differentiated
p whose stem runs obliquely down-left into a curled tail (pro loop), clearly different from the scribe's plain p; nobis suspended after b at line end
z-sign for final -m after u at line end; short tail; z/semicolon sign after a letter other than q, here = final -m
in 'presta' between p and a stands an x-shaped sign (r-rotunda-like body crossed by a diagonal hairline, resembling the rum sign); apparently abbreviates -res-/-rest-; unusual
